Discover Board Game Arena Rules summary Contents 1 Overview 2 Game rules 2.1 Word chain rules in English 2.2 Reverse word chain rules in English 2.3 Reverse word chain rules in German 2.4 Word chain rules in Japanese 3 Optional rules for prohibitions 3.1 Prohibiting to repeat the same letter 3.2 Prohibiting to end & start past chaining letters 4 Tips Overview "Illustori"(イラストリー) is a word chain game where you name artwork cards. The artwork name that the turn player chooses can be a sentence, a quote, an onomatopoeia, or anything. All it needs for chaining is the agreement from the other players. The language option is important . Please choose a language that all players can understand. Game rules The first player can choose any word or phrase that represents their card, but the other players get to vote to accept or reject it. No player cards are reduced by the action. On each player's turn, they play one of the following actions: Select a card and input its name that chains the last artwork name. Select one or more cards and swap them. If they chained the artwork name, all players discuss where the name matches the artwork or not. After that, everyone (excluding the turn player) vote if they agree the naming fits. If at least half of players agreed, the word chain succeeded! The next player should chain artwork name with the succeeded one. If fewer than half of players agreed, the word chain failed. The turn player discards the played card and draws a new card. The next player should continue with the previous artwork name. Once someone places all their cards, that will be the last round. The game ends once the player who decided the first artwork name finished their turn. All players who placed all their cards win the game! Word chain rules in English These are the original rules for BGA that is easier than the one in the game's manual. Input artwork name's first and last letter with alphabet. The next artwork name should start with the previous artwork name's last two letters. ex: Moon Next name starts "o" or "n". If you play with a prohibition rule, The next artwork name should start with the previous artwork name's last letter. The player (maybe its very rarely...) who names an artwork using a word that ends with 'xx' will get a penalty. They should discard the played card and draw a new card from the stack. Reverse word chain rules in English Input artwork name's first and last letter with alphabet. The next artwork name should end with the previous artwork name's first letter. ex: Moon Next name ends "m". There are no penalty rules. Reverse word chain rules in German Most of the rules are similar to ones in English. Input artwork name's first and last letter with German alphabet (which includes umlaut letters and Eszett). The next artwork name should end with the previous artwork name's first letter. ex: Monat Next name ends "m". Umlauts and Eszett have alternatives. "ä" can be replaced with "a". "ü" can be replaced with "u". "ö" can be replaced with "o". "ß" can be replaced with "s". The player who names an artwork using a word that starts with 'q', 'x' or 'z' will get a penalty. They should discard the played card and draw a new card from the stack. Word chain rules in Japanese Input words' first and last letter with Katakana or Hiragana. The next artwork name should start with the last letter of the last artwork name. ex: つきよ Next starts "よ". Some letters have alternatives. ex1: ばしゃ Next name starts "や". ex2: やかた Next name starts "た" or "だ". ex3: ラッパ Next name starts "は", "ば", or "ぱ". If the last letter of the artwork name was chōonpu, the very last letter becomes the starting letter. ex: ピッチャー Next starts "や". The player who names an artwork using a word that ends with 'ん' will get a penalty. They should discard the played card and draw a new card from the stack. community_text:
[Rating: 1/10] Worse game I have ever played, would rather try suffocate myself to death.  If there was any game to kill the mood, this would be it.   Pros: Allows you to know which friends you do not want to invite to your boardgame sessions  Cons:  Valid answers get rejected for no reason,  If you don't want someone to win, nothing to stop you rejecting all their answers No time limit for players to think of their idea, the downtime of this massive for everyone involved

[Rating: 1/10] An activity. A riff on the old country naming game, where the next country must start with the ending letter of the previous one but this uses illustrations which require a word association.  More a social activity than a game.  The Japanese version works slightly differently due to its syllables.

[Rating: 3/10] Honestly feels a lot like the loose-y goose-y rules of a Jackbox game but with significantly less fun or challenge.

[Rating: 4/10] A curious spin on the old "name a country/person/X that starts with the last letter of the previous move" game, the category instead being a hand of cartoon illustrations that you have to shed one by one. An amusing enough activity, but far too much luck in how relevant your hand is, and very much at the mercy of the group's generosity. (Suggested house rule given the opacity of what should count as a title: has to be the kind of thing you'd see in a crossword clue answer.)

[Rating: 4/10] As much a social activity as a game. There isn't really a game mechanism here, but the illustration style is lovely and approachable. To make it more fun and challenging, take an "exquisite corpse" approach and require each player's card to contribute to a continuous story, explaining how all the items chain together.
